In real estate law, there are a number of ways to acquire access to land. There is nothing to prevent the government from using private, more conventional means to acquire the use of land. Leases and right of way arrangements are but two means. However, in more long-term permanent situations, eminent domain is usually the preferred method since there is finality in the relationship. Additionally, high dollar government projects that traverse many properties cannot be held hostage or disrupted by a few hold-out owners. Eminent domain is not stealing property since property owners are entitled to be compensated at FMV by the government. It is often unsettling for property owners to give up land to the government they own in fee simple and have become very attached to, but it is hard to come up with a better means of doing it. Roadway acquisition in this country is much more disruptive because many of our public roads run right through the middle of farm and ranch land masses.
